text:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — carving R3 slice for Optimize toolkit. Customers keep asking for concrete batching heuristics + lightweight quant recs + eval-triggered alerts. Need to lock scope for the next sprint. Thoughts?
Alex Kim: echo — infra capacity is tight. If we enable aggressive batching we risk p99 spikes. Need SLO tradeoffs.
Pranav Reddy: propose 3 buckets for R3: 1) batching heuristics (pilot rules + telemetry), 2) quant recommendations (safe presets: fp16, int8 ff-only), 3) eval-alerts MVP (signal-level rules). Keep each piece minimum viable.
Luis Ortega: +1. Customer ask from Fintech A: want audit logs + explainable recs. That pushes quant recs to include rationale text (one-liner why). Can we include that in MVP?
Samira Chen: explainability is heavy. Suggest for R3 quant recs include a short templated rationale we generate from rule metadata, not model introspection. 
Alex Kim: also note runtime constraints: quant decision path must be offlined — no per-request model switching. We can serve recommendations as guidance only (non-blocking) to start.
Maya Patel: good. So acceptance criteria drafts: - Pilot with 3 customers onboarded, - p99 latency regression <= 10% vs baseline, - token cost reduction >= 15% for customers who adopt recs, - eval-alert FP rate < 5% in pilot. Any pushback?
Pranav Reddy: add: deployment gating: feature flags per-customer + metrics visible in Console (cost delta + alert counts).
Luis Ortega: also need runbook for alert escalation. Customer support will want SLA on noisy alerts.
Samira Chen: metrics we need in Console: per-route token delta, p50/p95/p99 latency, alert precision/recall (estimate). I'll sketch telemetry events.
Maya Patel: actionable scope cut suggestion: make batching heuristics the top priority (highest ROI), quant recs as advisory (docs + console recommendations), eval-alerts as lightweight signal-based alerts (no autopruning). That keeps runtime changes minimal.
Alex Kim: engineering owners: assign eng-runtime for batching (Pranav volunteer?), eng-infra for telemetry pipeline (Luis?), eng-platform for console work (Samira?).
Pranav Reddy: happy to own runtime batching heuristics prototype this sprint. Will deliver a policy DSL + example heuristics.
Luis Ortega: I'll own telemetry pipeline and pilot onboarding checklist.
Samira Chen: I'll own Console surfaces and the metrics dashboard mock.
prod-bot: Poll created — "R3 priority order" — options: [Batching, Quant advisories, Eval-alerts]. Vote pls: https://redwood.internal/poll/8253
Alex Kim: vote: Batching > Eval-alerts > Quant.
Maya Patel: OK final decisions: R3 MVP = batching heuristics (hard enable), quant recommendations (advisory only), eval-triggered alerts (MVP read-only alerts). Owners: Pranav, Luis, Samira.
Maya Patel: Draft milestones: Week 1: design + DSL spec, Week 2: prototype runtime heuristics + telemetry hooks, Week 3: console mock + pilot onboarding, Week 4: pilot rollout to 3 customers + metrics review.
Luis Ortega: noted dependencies: need trace-forward telemetry from serving runtime — eng-infra to prioritize.
Pranav Reddy: blocker: kernel-level batching change might need perf bench. I'll surface a perf-run request by EOD.
Samira Chen: I'll prepare dashboard mock and link in the doc: <https://redwood.ai/docs/optimize/r3-slice|R3 spec draft>.
Maya Patel: thanks team. If no objections by EOD we ship this as R3 scope. :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: +1
Pranav Reddy: +1
Luis Ortega: +1
Samira Chen: +1
